name: Can you frame a basement if there is minor moisture or dampness?

mainEntity.name: Can you frame a basement if there is minor moisture or dampness?

acceptedAnswer.text: Basement wall framing should only take place after any moisture issues, foundation seepage, or water intrusion are completely resolved. Installing wood framing or insulation against damp concrete can trap moisture, leading to mold growth, musty odors, and rot. Homeowners should inspect foundation walls after heavy rain or snowmelt, test slab moisture, and repair any active leaks before framing begins. Our team checks for dry conditions before installing treated bottom plates and setting up your perimeter framing layout.
acceptedAnswer.description: No, all basement water intrusion and foundation moisture must be permanently resolved before framing to prevent wood rot and mold buildup behind finished walls.
